psychology.dragonfly: Extreme selling pressure was completely absorbed by aggressive buyers.
psychology.gravestone: Bulls tried to rally but got violently rejected back to the opening price.
psychology.long_legged: Massive battle on both sides ending in complete stalemate.
psychology.hammer: Strong buying absorption at session lows rejected further downside.
psychology.shooting_star: Sellers overwhelmed the upward drive and forced the close near the lows.
psychology.marubozu: Unrelenting institutional momentum from open to close with zero hesitation.
psychology.spinning_top: Neither side has directional conviction; prepare for consolidation or potential reversal.
psychology.bullish: Bulls won the session and pushed the close higher than open.
psychology.bearish: Bears controlled the session and pushed the close below open.

candlestick_simulator.golden_rule_description: The body size represents dominant momentum conviction, while wick length reveals liquidity rejection and the intensity of the struggle between buyers and sellers.
candlestick_simulator.title: Interactive Candlestick Lab
candlestick_simulator.description: Adjust the OHLC sliders or select presets to view real-time candle anatomy, wick-to-body ratios, and market sentiment interpretations.

head-and-shoulders.name: Head & Shoulders
head-and-shoulders.description: Bears break the critical neckline support after buyers exhaust at the central head peak.
head-and-shoulders.pro_tip: Measure the target from the Head peak to the Neckline, then project it downward from the breakdown.

inverse-head-and-shoulders.name: Inverse Head & Shoulders
inverse-head-and-shoulders.description: Buyers overcome neckline resistance following final seller capitulation at the inverse head trough.
inverse-head-and-shoulders.pro_tip: Waiting for a 4H/Daily close above the neckline and a valid retest offers the best Risk:Reward.

double-top.name: Double Top ("M")
double-top.description: Two failed attempts to break upper resistance trigger swift liquidation down to measured targets.
double-top.pro_tip: If Peak 2 has lower volume than Peak 1, the success probability can reach 80%.

double-bottom.name: Double Bottom ("W")
double-bottom.description: Sellers fail twice to print lower lows, creating strong floor support before an explosive rally.
double-bottom.pro_tip: A neckline breakout with a volume spike confirms valid institutional accumulation.

bull-flag.name: Bull Flag
bull-flag.description: High-momentum impulse pole followed by orderly consolidation channel before upward continuation.
bull-flag.pro_tip: Project a target equal to 100% of the flagpole height from the upper-channel breakout.

ascending-triangle.name: Ascending Triangle
ascending-triangle.description: Buyers continuously buy at higher lows while pressing against horizontal ceiling resistance.
ascending-triangle.pro_tip: Volatility compression near the triangle apex can produce a strong breakout squeeze.

chart_simulator.title: Breakout Geometry & Measured Move Simulator
chart_simulator.description: Simulate measured move 1:1 price targets, neckline invalidation, Risk:Reward ratios, and volume breakout quality in real-time.

hammer.name: Hammer
hammer.description: A bullish reversal pattern appearing at the bottom of a downtrend with a long lower shadow and a small body near the high.
hammer.psychology: Sellers aggressively pushed prices to new lows, but strong institutional buying stepped in, rejecting lower prices and driving the close near the session high.
rules: Appears after a defined downtrend or pullback to key support.
Lower shadow must be at least 2x the height of the real body.
Little to no upper shadow.
Color of the body can be green (stronger) or red.
hammer.volume_rule: High or above-average volume on the hammer candle confirms institutional absorption.
hammer.entry_trigger: Buy on the break of the hammer candle high, or on a 50% wick retest.
hammer.stop_loss: 1-2 ticks below the lowest point of the lower shadow.
hammer.pro_tip: A green body hammer that forms right at a 200 EMA or daily support zone offers the highest probability setup.

shooting-star.name: Shooting Star
shooting-star.description: A bearish reversal pattern that forms after an uptrend, characterized by a long upper shadow and a small real body near the bottom.
shooting-star.psychology: Buyers drove price to new highs with optimism, but aggressive profit taking and institutional sellers absorbed the rally, closing near the open.
rules: Forms after a clear advance or at a major resistance ceiling.
Upper shadow must be at least 2x the height of the real body.
Little to no lower shadow.
Red body indicates stronger bearish dominance than green.
shooting-star.volume_rule: Volume spike at the top confirms exhaustion of retail buyers and smart money distribution.
shooting-star.entry_trigger: Sell / Short upon breaking below the shooting star low.
shooting-star.stop_loss: 1-2 ticks above the highest point of the upper shadow.
shooting-star.pro_tip: Look for shooting stars coinciding with RSI overbought (>70) or bearish divergence for high-confidence shorts.

inverted-hammer.name: Inverted Hammer
inverted-hammer.description: Bullish reversal pattern appearing at the bottom of a downtrend with a long upper wick, showing early buyer interest.
inverted-hammer.psychology: Bulls tested higher prices during the session. Although bears pushed it back down, bears were unable to make a new low, signaling shifting momentum.
rules: Appears at the end of a downtrend.
Upper wick is at least 2x the body length.
Small body near the session low.
Requires a strong bullish confirmation candle on the next session.
inverted-hammer.volume_rule: Higher volume signals accumulating interest from larger participants.
inverted-hammer.entry_trigger: Enter long only after the next candle closes ABOVE the Inverted Hammer high.
inverted-hammer.stop_loss: Below the low of the Inverted Hammer candle.
inverted-hammer.pro_tip: Never enter an inverted hammer without waiting for the next candle confirmation close.

doji.name: Doji (Standard, Dragonfly & Gravestone)
doji.description: A candle where the open and close are virtually equal, representing complete balance and indecision between bulls and bears.
doji.psychology: Neither buyers nor sellers could establish control by the session close. At key support or resistance, it signals a potential trend pause or reversal.
rules: Open and Close prices must be identical or extremely close (<0.1% difference).
Dragonfly Doji: Long lower shadow, no upper shadow (Bullish lean).
Gravestone Doji: Long upper shadow, no lower shadow (Bearish lean).
Long-legged Doji: Long shadows on both ends (High volatility indecision).
doji.volume_rule: Extreme volume on a Doji signifies a massive battle of liquidity before a major expansion.
doji.entry_trigger: Trade the breakout direction of the Doji high or low confirmed by subsequent candle close.
doji.stop_loss: Opposite end of the Doji shadow.
doji.pro_tip: Dojis are warning signs, not standalone buy/sell triggers. Always check the preceding trend and support/resistance context.

marubozu.name: Marubozu (Bullish & Bearish)
marubozu.description: A long candle with no shadows (or microscopic wicks), indicating total dominance from open to close.
marubozu.psychology: One side of the market controlled the action from the opening bell to the final tick with relentless momentum.
rules: No upper or lower wicks (or < 5% of total candle range).
Bullish Marubozu: Open = Low, Close = High (Solid Green).
Bearish Marubozu: Open = High, Close = Low (Solid Red).
Acts as strong continuation or key breakout confirmation.
marubozu.volume_rule: Heavy volume expands the validity of the momentum.
marubozu.entry_trigger: Enter on the close of the Marubozu or on a shallow 25-38.2% Fibonacci retracement.
marubozu.stop_loss: Beyond the midpoint (50%) or opposite boundary of the Marubozu body.
marubozu.pro_tip: The 50% midpoint of a Marubozu body often acts as strong dynamic support/resistance on future retests.

bullish-engulfing.name: Bullish Engulfing
bullish-engulfing.description: A strong two-candle reversal pattern where a large green candle completely engulfs the entire body of the previous small red candle.
bullish-engulfing.psychology: Bears opened price lower, but bulls overwhelmed supply with explosive buying volume, engulfing the entire previous day range.
rules: Must occur after a clear downtrend or at major horizontal support.
First candle is bearish (red).
Second candle is bullish (green) and its body completely covers the previous body.
Second candle open is equal to or lower than the first candle close.
bullish-engulfing.volume_rule: Volume on the green engulfing candle should ideally exceed the volume of the preceding candle.
bullish-engulfing.entry_trigger: Enter long on the close of the engulfing candle or on the breakout of its high.
bullish-engulfing.stop_loss: Below the lowest low of the two-candle formation.
bullish-engulfing.pro_tip: When an engulfing candle wraps around 2 or 3 previous candles, the reversal conviction is exponentially higher.

bearish-engulfing.name: Bearish Engulfing
bearish-engulfing.description: A premier two-candle bearish reversal pattern where a large red candle engulfs the preceding green candle at the top of an uptrend.
bearish-engulfing.psychology: Buyers opened high with optimism, but aggressive institutional sellers hit the bids, driving price down and erasing days of gains in one session.
rules: Must occur after a defined uptrend or at major resistance/supply zone.
First candle is bullish (green).
Second candle is bearish (red) and completely engulfs the prior body.
Close of the red candle is well below the open of the prior green candle.
bearish-engulfing.volume_rule: High volume on the red candle confirms institutional dumping/distribution.
bearish-engulfing.entry_trigger: Short upon close of the bearish engulfing candle.
bearish-engulfing.stop_loss: Above the highest high of the engulfing pair.
bearish-engulfing.pro_tip: Look for bearish engulfing candles reacting off a multi-week resistance or overbought RSI for optimal risk-reward trades.

tweezer-bottom-top.name: Tweezer Top & Bottom
tweezer-bottom-top.description: Two consecutive candles with identical highs (Tweezer Top) or identical lows (Tweezer Bottom), indicating price rejection at the exact same level.
tweezer-bottom-top.psychology: The market tested a critical support/resistance level twice on consecutive bars and was violently rejected each time.
rules: Tweezer Bottom: Two candles with identical lows at key support (Bullish).
Tweezer Top: Two candles with identical highs at key resistance (Bearish).
First candle aligns with current trend, second candle reverses direction.
Shadows touch the exact same price tier.
tweezer-bottom-top.volume_rule: Volume on the rejection candle should be substantial.
tweezer-bottom-top.entry_trigger: Enter on the break of the second candle extreme in the direction of the reversal.
tweezer-bottom-top.stop_loss: Beyond the matching tweezer wick levels.
tweezer-bottom-top.pro_tip: Tweezer levels create pinpoint, tight stop loss locations with exceptional risk-to-reward ratios.

piercing-line.name: Piercing Line & Dark Cloud Cover
piercing-line.description: Piercing line (bullish): opens below prior low and closes >50% into prior red body. Dark Cloud (bearish): opens above prior high and closes >50% into prior green body.
piercing-line.psychology: Traps breakout traders by gapping beyond previous extreme, then fiercely reversing to reclaim more than half of the previous momentum bar.
rules: Piercing Line: Occurs in downtrend, second green candle closes ABOVE the 50% midpoint of the first red candle.
Dark Cloud Cover: Occurs in uptrend, second red candle closes BELOW the 50% midpoint of the first green candle.
The deeper the penetration into the prior body (>60-70%), the more powerful the reversal.
piercing-line.volume_rule: Higher volume on the second piercing candle demonstrates real institutional accumulation/distribution.
piercing-line.entry_trigger: Enter on the close of the piercing candle or on the breakout of its high/low.
piercing-line.stop_loss: Below the lowest low of the piercing pattern (for Piercing Line).
piercing-line.pro_tip: If the second candle fails to close past the 50% midpoint, the pattern is considered weak and prone to trend continuation.

morning-star.name: Morning Star & Evening Star
morning-star.description: Gold-standard 3-candle reversal pattern: 1) strong trend candle, 2) small-bodied star showing exhaustion, 3) strong opposing candle confirming reversal.
morning-star.psychology: Day 1: Dominant trend continues. Day 2: Indecision and loss of momentum. Day 3: The opposite force explodes, overpowering the prior trend.
rules: Morning Star (Bullish): Long red candle -> Small body gap down -> Long green candle closing >50% into candle 1.
Evening Star (Bearish): Long green candle -> Small body gap up -> Long red candle closing >50% into candle 1.
The middle star candle can be green, red, or a doji (Morning Doji Star).
morning-star.volume_rule: Volume pattern: High on Candle 1 -> Low on Candle 2 (star) -> Surging volume on Candle 3.
morning-star.entry_trigger: Enter long (Morning Star) or short (Evening Star) on the close of the third candle.
morning-star.stop_loss: Below the low of the middle star candle.
morning-star.pro_tip: The Morning Star is one of the highest statistical edge patterns in classical technical analysis, especially on 4H and Daily timeframes.

three-white-soldiers.name: Three White Soldiers & Three Black Crows
three-white-soldiers.description: Three consecutive long-bodied candles closing progressively higher (White Soldiers) or lower (Black Crows) with small wicks, demonstrating sustained directional conviction.
three-white-soldiers.psychology: Sustained, continuous buying/selling pressure over three full sessions without meaningful pullbacks, proving that smart money has stepped in.
rules: Three consecutive bullish (green) or bearish (red) candles.
Each candle opens within or near the body of the previous candle.
Each candle closes at or near its high (soldiers) or low (crows).
Wicks must be relatively small.
three-white-soldiers.volume_rule: Volume should expand or remain elevated across all three consecutive candles.
three-white-soldiers.entry_trigger: Enter on the close of the 3rd soldier/crow or on the first subsequent minor pullback.
three-white-soldiers.stop_loss: Below the open/low of the first soldier candle.
three-white-soldiers.pro_tip: Beware of entering soldiers if the 3rd candle has an unusually giant body and RSI is already >80 (risk of exhaustion pullback).

rising-falling-three.name: Rising & Falling Three Methods
rising-falling-three.description: Elite continuation pattern: a long momentum candle followed by 3 small counter-trend consolidation candles kept within its range, completed by another massive trend candle.
rising-falling-three.psychology: After a big trend move, minor profit-taking occurs on low volume. The counter-trend forces are too weak to break the original range before the dominant trend resumes.
rules: Day 1: Strong long body in direction of trend.
Days 2-4: Three small counter-trend bodies that stay ENTIRELY within the high-low range of Day 1.
Day 5: Strong candle in original trend direction closing beyond Day 1 close.
rising-falling-three.volume_rule: High volume on Day 1, drying up during days 2-4 consolidation, then exploding on Day 5.
rising-falling-three.entry_trigger: Enter on the breakout close of the 5th candle.
rising-falling-three.stop_loss: Below the low of the 3-day consolidation range.
rising-falling-three.pro_tip: This is the classic "bull flag" translated into pure Japanese candlestick mechanics.

head-and-shoulders.name: Head & Shoulders
head-and-shoulders.description: The most reliable classical bearish reversal pattern, featuring a higher peak (head) between two lower peaks (shoulders) and a critical neckline support.
head-and-shoulders.psychology: Left shoulder forms as part of a normal uptrend. The head makes a new high, but with diminishing momentum. The right shoulder fails to make a higher high, signaling buyer exhaustion before neckline collapse.
structure_rules: Preceded by an extended, mature uptrend.
Head must be noticeably higher than both the Left and Right Shoulders.
Left and Right Shoulders should be relatively symmetrical in height and time.
Neckline connects the swing lows between the shoulders.
head-and-shoulders.neckline_rule: A decisive daily/4H candle close BELOW the neckline triggers the pattern activation.
head-and-shoulders.target_calculation: Target = Neckline Breakout Price - Vertical Height (Distance from Head Peak to Neckline).
head-and-shoulders.stop_loss_placement: Aggressive: Above the Right Shoulder high. Conservative: Just above the broken neckline (if retested).
head-and-shoulders.false_breakout_warning: Avoid shorting before the candle closes below the neckline; retail traders often get trapped by wick-only bounces.
head-and-shoulders.pro_tip: Right shoulders that take significantly longer to form than the left shoulder usually lead to deeper, faster selloffs.

inverse-head-and-shoulders.name: Inverse Head & Shoulders
inverse-head-and-shoulders.description: Premier bullish reversal pattern formed at the bottom of a downtrend with a central trough (head) lower than the two surrounding troughs (shoulders).
inverse-head-and-shoulders.psychology: Sellers make a final desperate attempt at the head, but fail to maintain downward momentum. The higher low on the right shoulder proves buyers have accumulated sufficient inventory to break resistance.
structure_rules: Appears after a protracted downtrend.
Head is the lowest point of the entire structure.
Right shoulder forms a higher low relative to the head.
Neckline acts as major resistance barrier.
inverse-head-and-shoulders.neckline_rule: Confirmed on candle close ABOVE the neckline resistance.
inverse-head-and-shoulders.target_calculation: Target = Breakout Price + Vertical Height (Distance from Head Lowest Low to Neckline).
inverse-head-and-shoulders.stop_loss_placement: Below the Right Shoulder low, or below the breakout candle low.
inverse-head-and-shoulders.false_breakout_warning: Wait for volume expansion on the neckline breakout to avoid getting trapped in sideways consolidation.
inverse-head-and-shoulders.pro_tip: Waiting for a retest of the broken neckline as new support improves win rate and tightens risk substantially.

double-top.name: Double Top ("M" Pattern)
double-top.description: Bearish reversal pattern consisting of two consecutive price peaks at nearly the same resistance level separated by a moderate trough.
double-top.psychology: Bulls push aggressively to the second peak but meet an overwhelming wall of institutional limit sell orders, failing to create a higher high.
structure_rules: Two peaks separated by at least 10-20 candles.
Peak 2 should not exceed Peak 1 by more than 1-2%.
The valley between peaks forms the baseline support (Neckline).
double-top.neckline_rule: Triggers when price closes below the central valley low.
double-top.target_calculation: Target = Neckline Price - Height of the Double Top.
double-top.stop_loss_placement: Above the highest peak, or above the midpoint of the right drop.
double-top.false_breakout_warning: Do not short at peak 2 prematurely before the neckline actually breaks.
double-top.pro_tip: If Peak 2 creates a bearish RSI divergence, the probability of a major collapse exceeds 80%.

double-bottom.name: Double Bottom ("W" Pattern)
double-bottom.description: Bullish reversal pattern resembling a "W", featuring two distinct swing lows at a shared support level followed by a breakout above the intermediate peak.
double-bottom.psychology: Bears attempt to break support a second time but find massive limit bids. The market rejects lower prices, creating a strong foundation for a trend reversal.
structure_rules: Two troughs formed at the same horizontal price zone.
Second trough often forms a slightly higher low or a liquidity sweep wick.
Central peak defines the breakout trigger level.
double-bottom.neckline_rule: Confirmed on a close above the intermediate swing high resistance.
double-bottom.target_calculation: Target = Breakout Price + Height from lowest trough to peak.
double-bottom.false_breakout_warning: Ensure the central peak is cleared with solid candle body close.
double-bottom.pro_tip: Look for the second bottom to form a bullish candlestick pattern like a Hammer or Engulfing for early low-risk positioning.

cup-and-handle.name: Cup & Handle
cup-and-handle.description: A powerful bullish continuation pattern shaped like a teacup: a rounded bottom consolidation (cup) followed by a shallow downward drift (handle).
cup-and-handle.psychology: The rounded cup represents steady institutional accumulation without panic. The handle represents mild, orderly profit-taking that shakes out weak hands before the explosive breakout.
structure_rules: Cup should have a smooth "U" shape, not a sharp "V".
Depth of the cup should typically be between 30% and 50% retracement of prior move.
Handle should retrace no more than 1/3 of the cup depth and slope downwards.
Breakout above the cup rim resistance confirms the trade.
cup-and-handle.neckline_rule: Entry triggers on candle close above the horizontal cup rim resistance line.
cup-and-handle.target_calculation: Target = Breakout Price + Vertical depth from cup rim to lowest point of the cup.
cup-and-handle.stop_loss_placement: Below the lowest point of the handle consolidation.
cup-and-handle.false_breakout_warning: Handles that drop deeper than 50% of the cup depth have a high probability of pattern failure.
cup-and-handle.pro_tip: Created by William O'Neil, this pattern is the cornerstone of leading growth stock and crypto mega-bull runs.

bull-flag.name: Bull Flag & Pennant
bull-flag.description: A sharp, almost vertical upward impulse (flagpole) followed by a tight, downward-sloping consolidation channel (flag) or converging triangle (pennant).
bull-flag.psychology: Aggressive buyers catapulted price upwards. Instead of dumping, the market consolidates tightly with minimal selling pressure as smart money refuses to let price drop.
structure_rules: Preceded by a steep, rapid pole with heavy volume.
Flag body slopes counter-trend (downwards) between two parallel channel lines.
Retracement in the flag should not exceed 38.2% to 50% of the flagpole.
Lasts usually between 5 to 20 bars.
bull-flag.neckline_rule: Triggers immediately when price breaks above the upper boundary trendline of the flag.
bull-flag.target_calculation: Target = Breakout Price + Height of the Flagpole (Measured Move).
bull-flag.stop_loss_placement: Below the lowest swing low of the flag channel.
bull-flag.false_breakout_warning: Do not chase if price breaks out with low/declining volume.
bull-flag.pro_tip: The tighter and shallower the flag consolidation, the more explosive the subsequent breakout rally.

bear-flag.name: Bear Flag
bear-flag.description: A sharp, rapid downward sell-off (flagpole) followed by a sluggish, upward-sloping consolidation channel (flag) before downward continuation.
bear-flag.psychology: Heavy selling hits the market. The weak bounce lacks institutional participation and volume, forming a liquidity pool for smart money to load short positions before the next drop.
structure_rules: Preceded by a steep plunge on heavy volume.
Flag channel slopes upwards against the dominant downtrend.
Consolidation does not retrace more than 50% of the drop.
bear-flag.neckline_rule: Confirmed upon breaking below the lower trendline of the flag channel.
bear-flag.target_calculation: Target = Breakdown Price - Length of the initial Flagpole.
bear-flag.stop_loss_placement: Above the highest swing high of the flag consolidation.
bear-flag.false_breakout_warning: Ensure the flag does not break above 50% Fibonacci retracement of the pole.
bear-flag.pro_tip: Bear flags in a high-volatility market often reach their measured move target much faster than bull flags.

ascending-triangle.name: Ascending Triangle
ascending-triangle.description: A bullish pattern characterized by a horizontal upper resistance line and an ascending lower support trendline forming higher lows.
ascending-triangle.psychology: Sellers are stubborn at a fixed price ceiling, but buyers are increasingly aggressive, willing to buy at ever-higher prices until the resistance wall is completely depleted.
structure_rules: Flat horizontal resistance with at least 2 distinct touches.
Ascending trendline with at least 2 higher swing lows.
Price gets squeezed towards the apex before the breakout.
ascending-triangle.neckline_rule: Triggers on a candle close above the horizontal resistance ceiling.
ascending-triangle.target_calculation: Target = Breakout Price + Widest vertical height of the triangle base.
ascending-triangle.stop_loss_placement: Below the most recent swing low within the triangle.
ascending-triangle.false_breakout_warning: Wick-only penetrations above resistance without body close are common fakeout traps.
ascending-triangle.pro_tip: Breakouts that occur between 60% and 75% of the distance to the apex have the lowest failure rates.

descending-triangle.name: Descending Triangle
descending-triangle.description: A bearish pattern featuring a horizontal support floor and a descending upper trendline forming lower highs, applying increasing downward pressure.
descending-triangle.psychology: Buyers defend a fixed price floor, but each rally is weaker than the last (Lower Highs). Eventually, buyers are exhausted and the floor collapses.
structure_rules: Flat horizontal support tested multiple times.
Descending upper trendline showing selling pressure on rallies.
Pattern typically resolves with a downward breakdown.
descending-triangle.neckline_rule: Triggers on candle close below the horizontal support floor.
descending-triangle.target_calculation: Target = Breakdown Price - Widest vertical height of the triangle.
descending-triangle.stop_loss_placement: Above the most recent lower high.
descending-triangle.false_breakout_warning: Check overall macro trend to ensure this is not an exhaustion bottom spring.
descending-triangle.pro_tip: Beware of descending triangles at the bottom of long bear markets; they can occasionally act as powerful double/triple bottom reversal springboards.

falling-wedge.name: Falling Wedge
falling-wedge.description: A bullish pattern where price is bounded by two downward-sloping, converging trendlines, signaling losing bearish momentum.
falling-wedge.psychology: Prices are making lower lows and lower highs, but the slope of the lows is flattening faster than the highs. Bears are losing grip, paving the way for a sharp upside squeeze.
structure_rules: Both upper and lower trendlines must slope downward.
The trendlines must converge towards an apex.
Can act as a bullish reversal (in a downtrend) or bullish continuation (in an uptrend).
falling-wedge.neckline_rule: Triggers on breakout and close above the upper descending trendline.
falling-wedge.target_calculation: Target = Breakout point + Height of the widest part of the wedge base.
falling-wedge.stop_loss_placement: Below the lowest point of the wedge structure.
falling-wedge.false_breakout_warning: Wait for candle close above the upper trendline rather than entering during intraday wicks.
falling-wedge.pro_tip: Falling wedges accompanied by bullish RSI divergence have among the highest statistical edge in swing trading.

moving-average-cross.title: EMA 20 / 50 / 200 Trend Alignment & Golden Cross
moving-average-cross.summary: The foundational trend-following framework used by hedge funds: trade only in the direction of the EMA 20 > EMA 50 > EMA 200 stack.
key_principles: EMA 20 represents short-term momentum; EMA 50 represents intermediate trend; EMA 200 represents institutional macro regime.
Golden Cross: EMA 50 crosses above EMA 200 (Long-term Bull Market trigger).
Death Cross: EMA 50 crosses below EMA 200 (Long-term Bear Market trigger).
Dynamic Support: During strong trends, price respects the EMA 20/50 band as a pullback bounce zone.
moving-average-cross.formula_or_setup: Bullish Alignment: Price > EMA 20 > EMA 50 > EMA 200. Entry on pullbacks to EMA 20/50 with confirmation candle.
action_checklist: Verify EMA slope is pointing upward at >30 degrees.
Wait for price to pull back to the dynamic zone between EMA 20 and EMA 50.
Look for a bullish candlestick pattern (e.g., Hammer or Engulfing) at the EMA.
Place Stop Loss below the EMA 50 or recent swing low.
Target at least 2:1 Risk-to-Reward ratio or ride the trend until price closes below EMA 50.
moving-average-cross.pro_tip: Never counter-trend trade against the EMA 200. The statistical win rate of long setups above the EMA 200 is over 35% higher than below it.

rsi-divergence-mastery.title: RSI Divergence: Regular Reversal & Hidden Continuation
rsi-divergence-mastery.summary: Detecting discrepancies between price action and momentum oscillator to anticipate impending reversals or powerful trend continuations.
key_principles: Regular Bullish Divergence: Price makes Lower Lows, but RSI makes Higher Lows (Signals major upside reversal).
Regular Bearish Divergence: Price makes Higher Highs, but RSI makes Lower Highs (Signals buyer exhaustion and downside reversal).
Hidden Bullish Divergence: Price makes Higher Lows, but RSI makes Lower Lows (Signals explosive trend continuation UP).
Hidden Bearish Divergence: Price makes Lower Highs, but RSI makes Higher Highs (Signals explosive trend continuation DOWN).
rsi-divergence-mastery.formula_or_setup: Divergence occurs when price slope and RSI oscillator slope disagree across at least 2 distinct swing points.
action_checklist: Identify two distinct price swings (Highs or Lows).
Check RSI values at the corresponding timestamps.
Confirm divergence angle (diverging or converging).
Wait for price action trigger: trendline break or candlestick confirmation.
Set invalidation Stop Loss just beyond the recent swing extreme.
rsi-divergence-mastery.pro_tip: Hidden divergence in the direction of the daily trend is one of the most profitable setups in technical analysis because you trade with institutional flow.

bollinger-squeeze-breakout.title: Bollinger Bands Squeeze & Volatility Expansion
bollinger-squeeze-breakout.summary: Trading the cyclical transition from low volatility contraction (The Squeeze) to explosive directional expansion.
key_principles: Markets oscillate between periods of low volatility (range contraction) and high volatility (range expansion).
The Squeeze: When upper and lower bands narrow to their tightest range in 20+ periods, a massive breakout is imminent.
Walking the Bands: In strong trends, price can hug the upper/lower band for extended periods.
%B Indicator: Measures relative price location between upper (1.0) and lower (0.0) bands.
bollinger-squeeze-breakout.formula_or_setup: Bandwidth = (Upper Band - Lower Band) / Middle Band. When Bandwidth hits a 6-month low, prepare for directional breakout.
action_checklist: Locate a prolonged Bollinger Squeeze where price is tightly coiling.
Check volume: low volume inside the squeeze is mandatory.
Wait for the first candle to close entirely OUTSIDE the upper (buy) or lower (sell) band with volume spike.
Enter on the breakout candle close.
Trailing Stop: Use the 20-period middle SMA line as your trailing exit.
bollinger-squeeze-breakout.pro_tip: Beware of the "Head Fake": a brief false breakout in one direction quickly followed by the real monster rally in the opposite direction.

smc-market-structure.title: Smart Money Concepts: Market Structure, BOS & CHoCH
smc-market-structure.summary: Read the market like institutional algorithms: identify Break of Structure (BOS), Change of Character (CHoCH), Order Blocks, and Liquidity Pools.
key_principles: Market Structure: Uptrend = Higher Highs (HH) + Higher Lows (HL). Downtrend = Lower Highs (LH) + Lower Lows (LL).
BOS (Break of Structure): Price breaks and closes beyond the previous swing high/low in the direction of the dominant trend (Trend Continuation).
CHoCH (Change of Character): Price breaks the most recent swing low in an uptrend (or swing high in a downtrend), signaling the first early warning of a structural trend flip.
Order Block (OB): The last opposing candle before an aggressive impulse move that created a market imbalance/gap.
Liquidity Sweeps: Smart money pushes price past retail stop loss clusters (equal highs/lows) to fill their massive positions before reversing.
smc-market-structure.formula_or_setup: Trade Setup: 1) Identify HTF Trend & Liquidity Sweep -> 2) Wait for LTF CHoCH -> 3) Place Limit Order at the unmitigated Order Block / FVG.
action_checklist: Map the swing highs and swing lows on the 4-Hour / Daily timeframe.
Mark the key liquidity pools (Equal Highs, Equal Lows, Trendline Liquidity).
Wait for liquidity to be swept with a long wick rejection.
Drop to the 15-Minute or 5-Minute timeframe to witness a clean CHoCH (body close).
Enter on the retest of the freshly created Order Block / Fair Value Gap.
Stop Loss placed tightly behind the Order Block invalidation point (yielding 1:3 to 1:10 R:R).
smc-market-structure.pro_tip: Do not trade every Order Block you see on the chart. An Order Block is only valid if it caused a clear Break of Structure (BOS) and left a Fair Value Gap (FVG).

atr-dynamic-risk.title: ATR Dynamic Stop Loss & Volatility Risk Management
atr-dynamic-risk.summary: The exact mathematical risk framework used inside RabaLaba Terminal: adaptive stop loss sizing calibrated to real-time market volatility.
key_principles: Fixed percentage stops (e.g. always 2% or $1) fail because market volatility changes constantly across different market regimes.
Average True Range (ATR, 14-period) measures the true market noise and average candle expansion.
Optimal Stop Loss distance = 1.5x to 2.0x ATR below the entry or structural support, giving the trade room to breathe without getting stopped out by random market noise.
Position Sizing Formula: Position Size = (Account Capital * Risk %) / (Entry Price - Stop Loss Price).
atr-dynamic-risk.formula_or_setup: Stop Loss = Entry Price - (ATR × 1.5). Position Units = (Account $ × Risk %) / (ATR × 1.5).
action_checklist: Read the current 14-period ATR value on your trading timeframe.
Calculate Stop Loss buffer = Current Price - (1.5 * ATR) for long positions.
Determine max acceptable dollar risk (e.g. 1% of a $10,000 account = $100).
Divide max dollar risk by the stop loss dollar distance to calculate exact position size.
Never increase position size if market volatility spikes; reduce size to maintain constant risk.
atr-dynamic-risk.pro_tip: Professional traders do not focus on how much they can make; they focus exclusively on position sizing and managing downside risk.

multi-timeframe-framework.title: Top-Down Multi-Timeframe Analysis (HTF -> MTF -> LTF)
multi-timeframe-framework.summary: The 3-tier timeframe alignment process: use High Timeframe for bias, Medium Timeframe for key levels, and Low Timeframe for sniper entry execution.
key_principles: Rule of 4-6x: The higher timeframe should be 4x to 6x larger than the lower timeframe (e.g. Daily -> 4H -> 1H or 4H -> 1H -> 15m).
HTF (Daily/Weekly): Establishes the macro narrative, key support/resistance zones, and institutional bias.
MTF (4-Hour/1-Hour): Identifies the market structure, swing highs/lows, and valid chart patterns.
LTF (15-Minute/5-Minute): Pinpoints precision entry triggers, candlestick confirmations, and minimizes stop-loss distance.
multi-timeframe-framework.formula_or_setup: HTF Trend: Bullish -> MTF Pullback to Support -> LTF Reversal Pattern (Hammer/Engulfing/CHoCH) = High-Probability Trade.
action_checklist: Step 1: Check Daily chart. Is price above EMA 200? Are we making Higher Highs?
Step 2: Check 4-Hour chart. Wait for price to pull back into a key Daily support level or EMA 50.
Step 3: Drop to 15-Minute chart. Look for a bullish candlestick pattern or break of structure.
Step 4: Execute on the 15-Minute candle close with Stop Loss below the local 15-Minute low.
Step 5: Target the Daily swing high for a massive 1:4+ Risk-to-Reward outcome.
multi-timeframe-framework.pro_tip: Never execute a trade on the lower timeframe that contradicts the dominant trend of the higher timeframe.

quiz-1.title: Candlestick Identification at Major Support
quiz-1.question: Price drops 8 sessions in a row into historical support. A small real body forms at top with lower shadow 3x body height and surging volume. What is the pattern and optimal action?

q1-a.text: Shooting Star. Open aggressive short position immediately.
q1-a.explanation: Incorrect. Shooting stars form at tops with upper shadow, not at support with long lower wick.

q1-b.text: Bullish Hammer. Open Long above the high with Stop Loss below the low.
q1-b.explanation: Correct! Small body at top with long lower wick signals selling absorption at support.

q1-c.text: Bearish Marubozu. Prepare for deeper downtrend continuation.
q1-c.explanation: Incorrect. Marubozu has full solid body with virtually no wicks.

q1-d.text: Gravestone Doji. Close all positions and hold cash.
q1-d.explanation: Incorrect. Gravestone Doji features a long upper wick, whereas this candle has lower wick.

quiz-1.pro_tip: Hammer candles with heavy volume at support hold historical win rates above 68%.

quiz-2.title: Chart Pattern Neckline Breakout Confirmation
quiz-2.question: Daily chart forms left peak at $100, middle peak at $115, and right peak at $101. Neckline connects troughs at $88. Candle closes at $85 on heavy volume. What is the pattern and target?

q2-a.text: Triple Top with projected downside target at $75.
q2-a.explanation: Incorrect. Middle peak is significantly higher than both outer peaks.

q2-b.text: Head and Shoulders with measured move target at $61.
q2-b.explanation: Correct! Measured move equals neckline breakdown $88 minus head height $27 to reach $61.

q2-c.text: Cup and Handle with upside target at $130.
q2-c.explanation: Incorrect. Cup and Handle is a bullish continuation, not a bearish topping pattern.

q2-d.text: Double Top with downside target at $80.
q2-d.explanation: Incorrect. Double Top only features two peaks of equal height.

quiz-2.pro_tip: Neckline retest at $88 provides optimal short entry with minimal risk exposure.

quiz-3.title: RSI Momentum and Divergence Detection
quiz-3.question: Bitcoin 1D chart prints new high at $98,000 above prior $92,000 peak. However RSI prints 64 versus prior peak reading of 79. What signal is shown on chart?

q3-a.text: Bullish Continuation because buying momentum is accelerating.
q3-a.explanation: Incorrect. Price Higher High with RSI Lower High indicates decelerating momentum.

q3-b.text: Regular Bearish Divergence signaling buyer exhaustion and potential sharp correction.
q3-b.explanation: Correct! Higher high in price with lower high in RSI is textbook Regular Bearish Divergence.

q3-c.text: Hidden Bullish Divergence projecting straight rally to $120,000.
q3-c.explanation: Incorrect. Hidden Bullish requires price Higher Low and RSI Lower Low.

q3-d.text: Neutral market condition with no technical indication.
q3-d.explanation: Incorrect. Momentum divergence is a premier leading reversal indicator.

quiz-3.pro_tip: Pair Daily Bearish Divergence with lower timeframe structure shift for high conviction entries.

quiz-4.title: Position Sizing and Risk Calculation
quiz-4.question: Capital is $10,000 with strict 1% risk limit per trade. Plan to buy ETH at $3,000 with Stop Loss at $2,850. What is the safe position size?

q4-a.explanation: Incorrect. 3.33 ETH risks $500 or 5% of account, violating 1% risk cap.

q4-b.text: 0.67 ETH with maximum dollar risk of $100.
q4-b.explanation: Correct! Max risk 1% of $10,000 is $100. Stop distance is $150. Sizing is $100 divided by $150 = 0.67 ETH.

q4-c.text: 1.00 ETH with total dollar risk of $150.
q4-c.explanation: Incorrect. 1 ETH risks $150 or 1.5% of account, breaching risk rules.

q4-d.explanation: Fatal mistake. Excessive position size creates immediate liquidation risk.

quiz-4.pro_tip: Calculating lot size from stop loss distance is key to long term capital survival.

quiz-5.title: Smart Money Concepts: Liquidity Sweep vs BOS
quiz-5.question: Price spikes above Equal Highs resistance but 4H candle closes back below with long upper wick. On 15M chart price instantly breaks previous swing low. What happened?

q5-a.text: Clean Break of Structure confirming uptrend continuation.
q5-a.explanation: Incorrect. Valid BOS requires full body candle closure above level, not wick rejection.

q5-b.text: Buy Side Liquidity Sweep followed by bearish Change of Character.
q5-b.explanation: Correct! Retail stop liquidity above equal highs was swept into institutional short fills.

q5-c.text: Healthy pullback in bull trend to buy immediately on market.
q5-c.explanation: Incorrect. Buying right after liquidity sweep and structure shift is a retail trap.

q5-d.explanation: Incorrect. No ascending triangle geometry exists in this scenario.

quiz-5.pro_tip: After HTF liquidity sweeps, seek short entries at unmitigated Order Blocks on LTF.

quiz-6.title: Shooting Star at Major Resistance Level
quiz-6.question: Asset rallies 5 straight sessions into multi month resistance. On day 6 candle prints upper shadow 3x body size and near zero lower wick. What is the best action?

q6-a.text: Buy aggressively because upper wick shows new price highs.
q6-a.explanation: Incorrect. Long upper shadow indicates severe selling rejection at peak.

q6-b.text: Anticipate Shooting Star reversal and protect downside with tight stop loss.
q6-b.explanation: Correct! Shooting Star at key resistance shows strong seller dominance and exhaustion.

q6-c.text: Open maximum leverage long without stop loss.
q6-c.explanation: Fatal mistake. Entering longs at resistance following shooting star risks wipeout.

q6-d.text: Ignore daily candle as formations carry zero meaning.
q6-d.explanation: Incorrect. Daily candlesticks are primary reference points for institutional market participants.

quiz-6.pro_tip: Shooting stars at key resistance with heavy volume carry reversal win rates above 65%.

quiz-7.title: Bullish Engulfing Confirmation at Support
quiz-7.question: Following sharp selloff, small red candle is fully engulfed by large green candle closing above prior high with volume surge. What pattern is this?

q7-a.explanation: Incorrect. Large green candle engulfing smaller prior red candle is Bullish Engulfing.

q7-b.text: Bullish Engulfing indicating buyer dominance and strong upward reversal.
q7-b.explanation: Correct! Bullish Engulfing at support backed by heavy volume is a high probability reversal trigger.

q7-c.text: Neutral Doji candle showing market hesitation.
q7-c.explanation: Incorrect. Wide range green candle demonstrates decisive directional momentum.

q7-d.text: Head and Shoulders bearish breakdown pattern.
q7-d.explanation: Incorrect. This two bar support trigger is an engulfing reversal formation.

quiz-7.pro_tip: Bullish Engulfing candles that engulf multiple previous bars carry superior continuation odds.

quiz-8.title: Double Bottom Reversal Validation
quiz-8.question: Daily chart prints two symmetrical troughs at $50 separated by peak at $65. When is optimal buy execution according to classical rules?

q8-a.text: Buy on initial touch of $50 on first bottom without confirmation.
q8-a.explanation: Suboptimal. Catching falling knives on first bottom fights active downtrend.

q8-b.text: Buy once price breaks and closes above $65 neckline.
q8-b.explanation: Correct! Double Bottom pattern is officially confirmed only upon neckline breakout.

q8-c.text: Short below $50 while price is rising toward $65.
q8-c.explanation: Incorrect. Shorting into developing base formation fights accumulating momentum.

q8-d.text: Wait for price to hit $30 without technical justification.
q8-d.explanation: Incorrect. No technical grounds exist to expect $30 in this formation.

quiz-8.pro_tip: Measured move target is vertical distance from trough $50 to neckline $65 projecting $80.

quiz-9.title: Bull Flag Continuation Following Impulse Move
quiz-9.question: Price surges 40% creating pole then consolidates downward within tight channel on drying volume. What pattern is this?

q9-a.text: Bull Flag continuation with measured move target matching pole height.
q9-a.explanation: Correct! Impulsive pole followed by low volume downward channel is textbook Bull Flag.

q9-b.text: Double Top long term trend reversal pattern.
q9-b.explanation: Incorrect. No twin peaks exist in pole and flag formation.

q9-c.explanation: Incorrect. Parallel channel after impulse is flag structure, not triangle.

q9-d.explanation: Incorrect. Death cross relates to moving average crossovers.

quiz-9.pro_tip: Declining volume during flag phase confirms healthy consolidation rather than distribution.

quiz-10.title: Geometric Ascending Triangle Dynamics
quiz-10.question: Chart shows flat resistance at $100 while swing lows print Higher Lows at $80, $88, and $94. What does this convey?

q10-a.text: Sellers dominate and price will drop below support.
q10-a.explanation: Incorrect. Higher Lows prove buyers absorb supply at progressively higher prices.

q10-b.text: Buying pressure is squeezing resistance at $100 with high upside breakout odds.
q10-b.explanation: Correct! Flat top with ascending lows forms classic bullish Ascending Triangle.

q10-c.text: Directionless chop with zero tradeable clarity.
q10-c.explanation: Incorrect. Consistent Higher Lows show systematic structural accumulation.

q10-d.explanation: Incorrect. Ascending triangle structure is completely distinct from topping pattern.

quiz-10.pro_tip: Ascending Triangles breaking upward carry average historical win rates over 70%.

quiz-11.title: Bollinger Bands Squeeze Volatility Strategy
quiz-11.question: Bollinger Bands squeeze to 3 month low bandwidth then price closes above Upper Band on surge volume. What is expected next?

q11-a.text: Price must mean revert to middle band immediately due to overbought levels.
q11-a.explanation: Incorrect. On squeeze breakout, walking upper band denotes powerful new trend impulse.

q11-b.text: Major volatility expansion and beginning of strong bullish trend.
q11-b.explanation: Correct! Squeezes represent compression; upper breakout triggers major trend expansion.

q11-c.text: Asset will stagnate without movement for months.
q11-c.explanation: Incorrect. Volatility squeeze consistently resolves into decisive expansion.

q11-d.text: Signal to open short positions without stop loss.
q11-d.explanation: Fatal mistake. Fighting post squeeze momentum expansion destroys account capital.

quiz-11.pro_tip: Breakout direction backed by surge volume after squeeze provides high momentum trigger.

quiz-12.title: Multi-Timeframe Analysis Confluence
quiz-12.question: Daily trend is bullish above EMA 200. 4H chart pulls back into buyer Order Block. 15M chart prints bullish CHoCH. What is best execution?

q12-a.text: Enter Long on 15M with Stop Loss below swing low for high R:R aligned with Daily trend.
q12-a.explanation: Correct! Ideal MTF confluence: Macro Trend 1D plus Value Zone 4H plus Micro Entry 15M.

q12-b.text: Short aggressively because 4H chart is moving downward.
q12-b.explanation: Incorrect. Shorting pullbacks within macro uptrends fights dominant order flow.

q12-c.text: Wait for Weekly candle to close before taking action.
q12-c.explanation: Suboptimal. Waiting for weekly close misses superior Risk to Reward entry window.

q12-d.text: Ignore lower timeframes as useless noise.
q12-d.explanation: Incorrect. Lower timeframes enable sniper entries and tighter risk bounds.

quiz-12.pro_tip: Top down framework from Daily trend to 4H location and 15M entry is pro standard.

quiz-13.title: Morning Star Three-Candle Reversal Pattern
quiz-13.question: In downtrend, large red candle appears on day 1, small body candle at base on day 2, and large green candle penetrating over 50% on day 3. What pattern is this?

q13-a.explanation: Incorrect. Evening star occurs at peak of uptrend, not at support base.

q13-b.text: Morning Star high probability three candle bullish reversal formation.
q13-b.explanation: Correct! Three candle reversal at support with deep green penetration is classic Morning Star.

q13-c.text: Three Black Crows extreme selloff signal.
q13-c.explanation: Incorrect. Three Black Crows consists of three consecutive red candles.

q13-d.text: Neutral Doji candle without directional bias.
q13-d.explanation: Incorrect. This three bar sequence displays decisive reversal dynamics.

quiz-13.pro_tip: Third candle penetration above 50% of first candle body confirms decisive buyer victory.

quiz-14.title: Classical Cup and Handle Continuation Pattern
quiz-14.question: Chart forms rounded bottom base (Cup) followed by shallow downward drift (Handle) below $120 resistance. What pattern is this?

q14-a.explanation: Incorrect. Rounded base accumulation differs fundamentally from double top peaks.

q14-b.explanation: Incorrect. Rounded bowl with shallow handle is a premier bullish continuation setup.

q14-c.text: Cup and Handle bullish continuation with measured target matching cup depth.
q14-c.explanation: Correct! Rounded accumulation followed by shallow handle forms classic Cup and Handle.

q14-d.explanation: Incorrect. This structure is among the most reliable continuation setups in technical analysis.

quiz-14.pro_tip: Handle retracements holding above 38.2% Fibonacci of cup depth denote immense underlying buying power.

quiz-15.title: Moving Average Trend Alignment Strategy
quiz-15.question: Price trades above ascending EMA 20, EMA 50, and EMA 200. Price pulls back into dynamic zone between EMA 20 and 50 then bounces. What setup is this?

q15-a.text: Trend Following Pullback Buy with Stop Loss below EMA 50.
q15-a.explanation: Correct! Stacked rising moving averages with pullbacks to dynamic value zone form premier trend entries.

q15-b.text: Open short position because price pulled back.
q15-b.explanation: Incorrect. Shorting into stacked bullish moving averages fights dominant macro momentum.

q15-c.text: Close all trading positions as trend is over.
q15-c.explanation: Incorrect. Dynamic EMA pullbacks are standard healthy behavior in ongoing trends.

q15-d.text: Target sell orders below EMA 200 baseline.
q15-d.explanation: Incorrect. EMA 200 acts as major institutional regime baseline.

quiz-15.pro_tip: Long win rates are substantially higher when price remains aligned above EMA 200 baseline.

quiz-16.title: Falling Wedge Bullish Reversal Formation
quiz-16.question: Price trends downward within two converging downward sloping trendlines with shallowing lower lows. What does this structure signify?

q16-a.text: Sellers gain power and price will collapse indefinitely.
q16-a.explanation: Incorrect. Converging wedge lines show seller momentum is gradually exhausting.

q16-b.text: Falling Wedge bullish reversal indicating diminishing downward momentum.
q16-b.explanation: Correct! Converging downward slope indicates accumulating demand ready for upside breakout.

q16-c.explanation: Incorrect. Converging boundaries define wedge structures rather than parallel flags.

q16-d.text: Neutral chop with zero future trajectory.
q16-d.explanation: Incorrect. Falling wedges possess strong statistical upside breakout probability.

quiz-16.pro_tip: Candle close breaking above upper falling trendline serves as optimal confirmation trigger.

quiz-17.title: Tweezer Bottom Support Reversal Pattern
quiz-17.question: At critical $45 support, red candle on day 1 and green candle on day 2 share exact identical low at $45.00 with lower wick rejection. What pattern is this?

q17-a.explanation: Incorrect. Tweezer tops occur at peaks, not at support floors in downtrends.

q17-b.explanation: Incorrect. Matching lows with green second candle is not bearish engulfing.

q17-c.text: Tweezer Bottom bullish reversal showing support defended twice.
q17-c.explanation: Correct! Consecutive identical lows at support confirm solid buyer defense.

q17-d.explanation: Incorrect. Rejection at identical support price levels validates structural base.

quiz-17.pro_tip: Tweezer bottoms coinciding with major Fibonacci or horizontal levels provide high probability reversal confirmation.

quiz-18.title: Smart Money Concepts: Order Block Retest Entry
quiz-18.question: Institutional buying triggers upward Break of Structure leaving Demand Order Block behind. Price drifts down into Order Block. What is optimal action?

q18-a.text: Place Buy Limit in Order Block zone with Stop Loss below OB box.
q18-a.explanation: Correct! Order Blocks triggering BOS represent institutional demand zones defending retests.

q18-b.text: Open immediate short position into the incoming Order Block.
q18-b.explanation: Incorrect. Shorting into unmitigated institutional demand risks severe bounce.

q18-c.text: Ignore OB zone because smart money never revisits old levels.
q18-c.explanation: Incorrect. Institutions regularly mitigate unfilled resting orders at Order Blocks.

q18-d.text: Close chart and avoid trading this setup.
q18-d.explanation: Incorrect. Retest into valid Order Blocks offers premier asymmetrical Risk to Reward ratios.

quiz-18.pro_tip: Unmitigated Order Blocks hold the highest statistical probability of responsive price reaction.
